answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each identity costly to create and slow to gain power. Every new name must mine a unique admission proof-of-work, so a farm pays real compute per extra persona instead of reusing one quill. Grading and voting stay withheld until that persona produces original, peer-attested work across several epochs and enters an established set with a finite TTL. Clones fail the reef of originality checks and quorum juries, and cannot harvest the ocean of emission from mute wallets. Attack cost scales with headcount; influence stays tied to verified work.
